top.title: Gov Mbah: How Tinubu’s reforms halted Nigeria’s economic collapse
top.description: …Says shared prosperity follows Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, says Nigeria would have suffered total economic collapse but for President Bola Tinubu’s courageous reforms, arguing that the removal of fuel subsidy and floating of the naira only waited until the President’s assumption of office in 2023 because the nation delayed the ‘evil day’ and lived on borrowed time. He gave the insights at the weekend during the launch of “As Tinubu Mbah Moves” (ATM), a support group convened by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Udeh (SAN), and dedicated to the re-election of President Tinubu and Governor Mbah in Enugu. Speaking to the mammoth crowd, he said, “It would have been a lot easier for any leader to just continue with the status quo and carry on on the basis of business as usual. But for Bola Ahmed Tinubu, it was business unusual that led to the bold initiatives. “As a person who had played very actively in the oil and gas sector, I had written quite a lot of features and articles arguing against the fuel subsidy regime long before now, for it was clear to me, even from the point of a major player in that sector, that the subsidy regime was not sustainable because of the economic devastation it was causing to us as Nigerians. We were just basically postponing the evil day. “We were just digging our poverty pits continually. We were actually digging deeper into that pit of poverty. And it would have taken a very courageous leader in his first term to say, ‘Look, if we have to build for the future, if we have to think about our children, then we must take out the subsidy and we must also unify the exchange rate regime.’” Mbah took a swipe at the foreign exchange regime before the floating of the naira by Tinubu, describing it as a cesspool of corruption. “We got to a point in this country where even salary earners, once they get paid, would run to the bureau de change to change it rather than hold their salary in naira. Confidence was completely eroded in the naira. Nobody wanted to touch it with the tip of their finger. And that was the recipe for a failed nation. “If you wanted to do a study or research of any failed nation, it is when the country, the citizens themselves, begin to lose confidence in their currency. And that was the environment that this President inherited. “It was a major cesspool of corruption. The arbitrage was obvious and people were being taken advantage of. What was happening between the official and the parallel market was terrible. And some people were benefiting from that arbitrage at the expense of the economy. But it took this President’s understanding of the economy to be able to make those bold decisions,” he explained. top.title: 'We did likewise': Mohit Ulva reveals why India celebrated aggressively after beating Pakistan
top.description: India U-19 batter Mohit Ulva has explained the emotions behind the team's animated celebrations following their dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final, insisting that the players were simply celebrating their triumph and had no intention of provoking their opponents. Mohit, who played a decisive role in India's remarkable chase with an unbeaten 49 off just 26 balls, said the celebrations were a natural reaction to the occasion, given the intensity of an India-Pakistan contest and the fact that it was a final. The celebrations that followed, however, became a talking point, with several Indian players facing criticism on social media for their aggressive gestures towards the Pakistani players. Mohit revealed that the celebrations were a spontaneous expression of the emotions surrounding an India-Pakistan final. He also recalled how the Indian youngsters had not taken Pakistan's celebrations during the league-stage encounter personally. "It is natural. It was an India vs Pakistan match, and additionally, a final. The way they celebrated after beating us in the league stage. Actually, we were not even taking their celebration personally. We were thinking that they were celebrating their own victory. It doesn't matter what they do. "We did likewise. We were celebrating our own victory. It had emotions, aggression, and everything. We weren't doing it to show them anything. We were celebrating among ourselves, and everything was natural," Mohit told Star Sports. 'I couldn't believe I had finished it' India were staring at defeat after slipping to 252/8 in the 42nd over of the chase. However, Mohit and Manal Chauhan refused to give up, putting together a crucial 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket to keep India's hopes alive. Manal scored 47 off 32 balls before departing, leaving India needing 36 more runs with just one wicket remaining. Mohit then received support from No. 11 C Venkata, who remained unbeaten on 11 off eight deliveries. The equation eventually came down to three runs off the final ball, with Mohit finding the boundary to seal the title. Recalling the extraordinary finish, the youngster admitted that he was initially unable to process what had happened. "Actually, I was completely zoned out after hitting three runs on one ball with a four. I didn't know that everyone was running to me; everything was happening. "It was done; I finished the game. Until it was over, I believed that I would finish it. But after I did it, I couldn't believe that I had finished it. So, I was a little zoned out. "After a while, I realised that it was actually over. Everyone was getting up, everyone was celebrating. So, I celebrated a little. I went to the supporters of India, who were sitting there the whole day. I went to them and celebrated with them. It's a very good feeling. Even now, it's a very good feeling for me. Because for my family, for my country, for India, it's a good feeling to win such a match," he added. '

top.title: Ciryl Gane Needs A Homecoming Fight In France After UFC 334
top.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Ciryl Gane walked out of Madison Square Garden with his UFC heavyweight title intact on Saturday night. He defeated Josh Hokit by unanimous decision, but the reception felt wrong for a fighter who just set a new record for strikes in a single heavyweight bout. Gane landed 298 total strikes and Hokit threw 243, for a combined 541 strikes, which ESPN reported as a division record. The Frenchman displayed skill, but fans in the arena treated him like a villain rather than a champion. UFC CEO Dana White admitted he once thought Hokit was a “bigmouthed goofball” before the fight took place. White changed his tune after seeing Hokit push the champion backward with relentless pressure throughout the five-round war. “I respect the s— out of that guy,” White said during the postfight news conference, adding that Hokit is the real deal. By enduring Gane’s volume and electrifying the crowd with a massive slam to close the first round, Hokit earned this respect. A Homecoming in France Gane has spent years playing the role of the bad guy, even after beating top contenders like Alex Pereira in June. He lost to Jon Jones in 2023 and faced controversy with Francis Ngannou in 2022, but his résumé proves he belongs at the top. The UFC should stop booking him in hostile markets and finally give him a fight in his home country of France. As one of the top pound-for-pound fighters globally, Gane has constructed an impressive record and merits a cheering crowd. The Tactical Mistake in the Co-Main While Gane won the main event, Amanda Nunes made a costly tactical error in the co-main event against Kayla Harrison. The former two-time champion returned from retirement but was outplayed by the reigning bantamweight champion, who imposed her own game. Despite possessing the striking ability and experience to win, Nunes could not dictate the pace or terms of the engagement. Hokit said in his postfight interview that he will “rejoice in my suffering.” He promised that even if people kick him when he is down, he will still break their leg one day. Gane credited Hokit’s approach after the bout, noting that the world took him lightly but not the champion himself. “This guy is a motherf—er,” Gane said about his challenger. Gane landed 237 significant strikes, shattering the UFC heavyweight record for a single fight.

top.title: Tottenham Hotspur Urged To Move In For This Arsenal Forward: Should De Zerbi Go For Him?
top.description: Tottenham Hotspur Urged To Move In For This Arsenal Forward: Should De Zerbi Go For Him? In a recent interview with The Last Word On Spurs , David Pleat urged his former club Tottenham Hotspur to move in for Arsenal forward Viktor Gyokeres. Pleat said, “There aren’t many out there; there’s a very small amount of strikers. “Are you going to buy Lankshear back now for £50 million? He’s the top scorer in the Championship, our boy. “So where are you going to get? Are Arsenal going to give us someone like Jesus, or someone they don’t want? He’s gone already, but Gyokeres, perhaps. Who else is there? “[Brian] Brobbey gave us trouble… [Dominic] Calvert-Lewin is very good in the air but had injury problems. When you are signing a striker, it’s about what type of striker. Is he exceptionally good in the air, is he a bully-type striker like Delap or is a clever front player, more like Havertz?” Gyokeres’ Growing Struggles In North London Gyokeres has struggled to earn regular first-team starts for Arsenal in this campaign so far as he has fallen behind Kai Havertz in Mikel Arteta’s pecking order. The 28-year-old registered two goals and three assists in 14 appearances for the Gunners this season in all competitions. The Swedish talent is currently among the most talented forwards in the Premier League. Hence, Tottenham would do well to bring him on board next year. LONDON, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 07: Viktor Gyokeres of Arsenal runs with the ball during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Arsenal FC and Hull City at Emirates Stadium on November 07, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) His current contract at the Emirates Stadium will run out in the summer of 2030, which could make it difficult for Spurs to land him on the cheap this January or at the end of this campaign. Should Tottenham Hotspur Boss Roberto De Zerbi Go For Gyokeres? Gyokeres is proficient at finding a yard of space for himself to get some strikes in at goal. He has the vision to engineer the odd chance for his teammates to score and is a decent dribbler with the ball at his feet. Standing at 1.89m, the Swedish forward is a strong presence in the air as well. However, there are some question marks on whether he can find a consistent run of form in the Premier League if Spurs manage to snap him up next year. We can expect Gyokeres to add more quality and depth to Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi’s frontline. He is capable of challenging for a regular first-team spot at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. At 28, Gyokeres is about to enter his prime, which makes him a decent choice for Spurs to pursue in 2027. Hence, Tottenham would be wise to go for a striker with his skill set soon.

top.title: LeBron James Returns For Sixers As Back-To-Back Looms
top.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James is set to return to the Philadelphia 76ers lineup for Sunday’s home game against the Indiana Pacers. The 41-year-old star missed Thursday’s victory over the Toronto Raptors to manage low back and sciatica issues, marking his third absence in the team’s first 13 games. This is a massive boost for a team that has struggled to find consistency without its veteran leader. The Sixers have been careful with James’ workload all season. He has not played on consecutive days yet this year as the team manages his health. Nick Nurse now faces a tough choice on how much to play him before the team travels to Brooklyn for a road game on Monday. James struggled in his last outing against Boston, scoring only 11 points on 4-of-12 shooting in 29 minutes. In his first season with the Sixers, he maintains averages of 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 6.5 assists across 10 appearances. His passing ability remains a key asset even if his scoring has dipped. A Tough Road Ahead The Pacers enter Sunday’s game looking for their third straight win after beating the New York Knicks in NBA Cup play on Friday. While dealing with their own injury concerns, Indiana has relied heavily on Pascal Siakam. The Sixers have managed to keep winning despite the heavy load on James and Joel Embiid. Tyrese Maxey led the team with 27 points in the win over Toronto, while Anfernee Simons added 17 off the bench. Rookie VJ Edgecombe also contributed 15 points, eight rebounds and eight assists in that game. Philadelphia has a difficult path in the NBA Cup after a heavy 24-point loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov. 6. That loss hurt their point differential significantly and put them behind in the group race. The team now needs big wins against tough opponents like the Heat and Pacers to stay in the hunt. Sixers Wire reports that the Sixers, Cavaliers, Heat, Knicks, and Pacers are among the teams battling for a next-round spot. The math for Philadelphia is unforgiving, and every point matters. Back-to-Back Concerns According to The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Chris Hine, Thursday’s absence was James’ first that was not related to a back-to-back schedule. This makes his availability for Monday’s game against the Brooklyn Nets a major question mark. The team must decide if playing Sunday is worth the risk of burning him out for the road trip. James has four full days of rest before Sunday, which gave him extra recovery time. LeBron James has not been officially confirmed as a starter yet, though his absence from the injury report suggests he is expected to play.

top.title: Blues Offense Stalls Again In Ugly Loss To Florida
top.description: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images A 4-1 loss to the Florida Panthers on Saturday night meant the St. Louis Blues could not achieve three straight wins. This loss dropped the team to 9-9-2 on the season, a record that makes it hard to call them a true contender. Jacob Markstrom recorded 21 saves for Florida as Dylan Holloway netted the single goal for St. Louis. Joel Hofer stopped 24 shots, but it was not enough to keep the game close. A Special Night with Ugly Results Saturday was supposed to be about celebrating Keith Tkachuk. Supporters had a chance to celebrate a legend as the Blues recognized his Hockey Hall of Fame induction. His sons, Matthew and Brady, played for the Panthers that night, adding a personal touch to the ceremony. Robert Thomas even wore a Tkachuk jersey to the arena, a nod to the time he lived with the family. The ceremonial faceoff used sticks Keith actually used during his career. It was a great moment for the family and the fans, but the result on the ice was a disaster. The team could not translate that emotional energy into goals. Offense Just Does Not Exist The Blues struggled to generate anything offensively from the start, managing just two shots on goal in the first period. Florida had 10 shots, and they capitalized on a pair of penalties to take an early lead. Brady Tkachuk opened the scoring with a toe drag, beating Hofer glove-side. Dmitry Kulikov made it 2-0 after a deflection off Colton Parayko’s stick. The second period offered no help, as St. Louis failed to register a single shot on its power play. For the seventh time this season, the Blues managed to score one goal or fewer. According to The Hockey News , they have now been outscored 16-6 in the four games where they tried to win three straight. “It’s something we’re trying to work on, right,” Blues forward Jake Neighbours said. “I wish I had the answer for you,” Neighbours added after playing in his 300th NHL game. Defense Breaks Down Fast Defensive mistakes doomed the Blues before the offense could even try to fix them. The Panthers scored early and often, building a lead the Blues could not chip away at. Anton Lundell added a goal in the second period, and Sam Reinhart made it 4-1 in the third with a slick move past Parayko. With one game remaining before the quarter mark, the team currently trails the second wild card spot in the Western Conference by three points. “More intensity and driving the net harder and getting pucks there more often,” Blues coach Jim Montgomery said. The team has two days to regroup before their next game. The Blues will look to finish off this two-game homestand strong when they come back Tuesday against Anaheim.

top.title: SDSU men's basketball goes to 4-0 after beating Northern Colorado
top.description: South Dakota State men's basketball moved to 4-0 on the season after a dominant display in Rapid City on Saturday, Nov. 14, beating Northern Colorado 71-46. The 4-0 start is the Jackrabbits' best since 2015-16, when they started 6-0. South Dakota State plays Mayville State and Idaho State to tie that record, then a home game against Abilene Christian could surpass it. It wasn't an offensive showcase on either side, but South Dakota State's defense held Northern Colorado to 26.5% (13-for-49) from the field. The Bears were just 3-for-22 (13.6%) from three. The Jackrabbit offense wasn't incredible, but Jon Mekonnen, Joe Sayler and EJ Ryans all scored in double figures. The trio scored 14, 13 and 10 points, respectively. Mekonnen added 11 rebounds, while Sayler had six assists. Davis Kern pitched in nine points and Alec Squires had eight points and eight boards. South Dakota State will look to make it 5-0 at home against Mayville State at 7 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 16. top.title: NASCAR Drivers Lose Power Over Crew Chief Changes
top.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Two of the biggest names in NASCAR admitted they had no voice in recent crew chief changes. Alex Bowman and Shane van Gisbergen confirmed they were not consulted before their teams swapped leaders. The moves happened right after the 2026 season ended, leaving drivers to accept new bosses they did not choose. This shift shows a clear power gap between the people behind the wheel and the teams that hire their staff. Drivers Feel Shut Out Alex Bowman, who is wrapping up his final Cup season in 2027, lost Blake Harris as his crew chief. Harris is moving to Trackhouse Racing to lead Shane van Gisbergen’s team. Bowman told Autoweek he was not part of the decision-making process. When questioned regarding his participation in the crew chief situation, “I haven’t really been a part of that,” Bowman replied, according to Autoweek . He added that other people likely have a better view of the changes. The Arizona native noted that not every race team operates the same way, which makes finding the right fit harder for drivers. Van Gisbergen faces a similar reality with his own crew chief, Stephen Doran, returning to Spire Motorsports. He described the process as simply accepting who you get and making it work. “You kind of just get put with who you are and work it out from there,” Van Gisbergen said. He believes the final call rests entirely with the team owners and managers. Why Leadership Matters More Because of this, he needs a crew chief who can step up and make tough calls. “I’m not the most natural leader in the world,” Bowman said. He explained that having a strong leader in the booth is vital for his success. “I’m shy and awkward and kind of stick to myself. So having a good, strong leader as a crew chief is important.” The changes ripple through the organization. Spire offered a team-wide engineering role to Travis Peterson, who had been Michael McDowell’s crew chief. Meanwhile, Austin Dillon will also have a new crew chief in 2027. Richard Childress Racing now has Richard Boswell as vice president of competition; he served Dillon for the last two seasons. These shifts happen fast, and the drivers are left to adapt or accept the outcome. Van Gisbergen summed up the situation with a simple statement about where the power lies. “It’s up to the team, I guess,” Van Gisbergen said. While not really formally holding a GM title, Grabiner had run the White Sox in tandem with three generations of Comiskey ownership, dating back to 1915. He first caught on with the team in 1905, selling scorecards; the 15-year-old got the job after noticing owner Charles Comiskey working the Comiskey Park infield after a rainstorm and asking if he could help out. By 1916, Grabiner was the team secretary (the de facto GM), at just 26. In 1939 upon the death of Comiskey’s son, Louis , the will stipulated that Grabiner was guaranteed another 10 years of employment in running the White Sox. However, Grabiner’s health was in decline, forcing his leave six years later. Grabiner would soon return to baseball, as part of Bill Veeck ’s ownership group in Cleveland. Meanwhile in Chicago, sabermetrics pioneer Les O’Connor took over the club for the next three seasons. Also on this day came some administrative news of a different sort. With Hall of Fame voting at this time occurring just once every three years, just one player and two people overall had been elected to the Hall of Fame over the previous five years. With a massive pileup of worthy players were clogging the ballot, Cooperstown decided to hold a runoff election in order to get more players into the Hall — but the move was ineffective, as no one reached the necessary 75% for election. That included legendary White Sox hurler Ed Walsh , who received just 137 of 247 (55.5%) of votes, finishing third overall on the ballot. 1948 After six years with the White Sox (interrupted right in the middle by three seasons lost to military service in World War II), Taffy Wright was sold to Philadelphia. By 1948, with the right fielder’s WAR winnowed down to 0.5 over a full season of play, Chicago cut ties. He would play one subpar season for the Athletics and would not see the majors again, although Wright would stay active in the minors until 1956, at age 44. 1951 In an outrageous turn, White Sox outfielder Minnie Miñoso lost the American League Rookie of the Year award to Gil McDougald of the New York Yankees , 13 votes to 11. nigeria.description: By Adeola Badru The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, have called for national healing, peaceful co-existence and stronger bonds among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups, warning that the politicisation of traditional institutions poses a threat to their stability, historical relevance and role in fostering national unity. The two prominent traditional rulers made the call on Sunday in Ibadan when Sanusi paid a courtesy visit to Oba Ladoja at his palace in Oke-Aremo, Ibadan, in an engagement that highlighted the need for traditional institutions to rise above partisan interests and serve as instruments of reconciliation, mutual understanding and national cohesion. Sanusi, who was in Ibadan to honour an invitation from the League of Imams and Alfas in South-West Nigeria, said his visit reflected his belief in a country where ethnic background, religious affiliation and political differences would not determine relationships among citizens. He described the engagement as part of the positive developments needed to bridge Nigeria’s regional and cultural divides, stressing that the country could only achieve unity, progress and prosperity when people from different backgrounds deliberately reached out to one another. The Emir explained that although other engagements had emerged, he considered it important to honour his earlier commitment to attend the conference, even if his participation would be brief. “We fixed this date a long time ago, and even though other events came, we considered it important to honour our promise to appear at the conference, even if it is for a brief period, because they have been expecting me to come.“ “This invitation is part of the positive developments we have been yearning for to build a bridge where Nigerians from different parts of the country reach out to each other and come together in the interest of the unity, the progress and the prosperity of our dear nation,” Sanusi said. nigeria.title: Gunmen kidnap three travellers, shoot driver on Benue highway
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru Armed men have reportedly kidnapped three travellers and shot a driver during an attack on a vehicle at Ijami village, Oglewu, Ohimini Local Government Area, LGA, of Benue State. The incident, which occurred at about 9:25pm on Saturday, involved seven persons travelling from Enugu to Abuja. The latest attack came barely days after a similar incident along the same axis, where a grieving man and his five friends were kidnapped while conveying the remains of his late wife from Kano for burial in neighbouring Okpokwu Local Government Area. In that incident, the kidnappers reportedly abandoned the corpse of the deceased on the highway before whisking her husband and his friends into the forest. They were subsequently released after a ransom was paid. Recounting the latest incident, an eyewitness, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the victims were attacked shortly after passing Otukpo on their way to Abuja. He said, “they were coming from Enugu and heading to Abuja on Saturday. At about 9:25pm, they got to a place called Ijami after Otukpo, under Oglewu. They were seven persons in the vehicle. The vehicle was attacked and the driver was shot. “He is in critical condition and currently receiving treatment in a hospital. Three of the passengers were taken into the forest by the armed men, while three of the passengers managed to escape. They have been seen and are in safe condition.” Expressing concern over the recurring attacks along the route, the eyewitness appealed to motorists to avoid travelling on the axis at night, blaming the deplorable condition of some roads for making it easier for criminals to operate. “We will continue to appeal to people to avoid these routes when night falls. Some of these roads are in deplorable condition, which makes it easy for the criminals to stop the vehicles and take away their victims. “We appeal that wherever you are coming from, pass the night in Otukpo and continue your trip the next day and be safe, rather than end up in the hands of armed men who will subject your family to unimaginable trauma to raise ransom money,” he said. Efforts to get the reaction of the Chairman of Ohimini Local Government Area, Gabriel Adole, were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to calls put across to his telephone. However, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, confirmed the incident. He said, “The victims were seven in number, three were rescued while three others are with the kidnappers. The driver was shot and he is receiving treatment at Teaching Hospital, Otukpo. “While efforts are on to secure the release of the other three, we urge the commuters to avoid night travels. Whenever it is night, look for somewhere and pass the night. The Commissioner had issued that advice and we expect that people, for their own safety, desist from night travels.” Vanguard News The post Gunmen kidnap three travellers, shoot driver on Benue highway appeared first on Vanguard News .

business.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Nvidia is due to report third-quarter results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, the first earnings release since Huang stepped down. entertainment.title: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar Makes History as First Female Vice-Chancellor of UNIJOS
entertainment.description: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar, appointed as the 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor and first female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos. The University of Jos (UNIJOS) has officially appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the institution was established in 1971. Announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026 by the university’s Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent , during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council, the historic appointment sees Professor Lar succeed Professor Tanko Ishaya as she takes the helm of the Plateau State institution. Born in Langtang, Plateau State, Professor Lar is a distinguished Professor of Medical Microbiology whose career has been deeply woven into the fabric of UNIJOS for nearly four decades. After earning her Bachelor of Science degree in Microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1986, she joined the University of Jos in 1987 as a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Medical Microbiology. She later went on to earn her Master’s degree in Medical Microbiology in 1989 and her PhD in Medical Parasitology in 1998 from the University of Lagos, followed by postdoctoral training at the Institute of Human Virology, University of Maryland in the United States under the NIH-Fogarty Fellowship Programme. Rising steadily through the academic ranks, she became an Associate Professor in 2012 before attaining full professorship in October 2015. Over the years, she has built an impressive body of work with more than 40 scholarly publications focusing on infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS, malaria, antimicrobial resistance, and phytomedicine. Beyond the lecture hall and laboratory, Professor Lar has also served in key administrative roles at UNIJOS—including Head of the Department of Microbiology and Director of Linkages and Collaborations—and previously served a six-month tenure as Acting Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University (formerly the University of Abuja) following her appointment by President Bola Tinubu in February 2025. Alongside her academic and leadership credentials, Professor Lar is a recognised advocate for women’s empowerment, having received the He4She Certificate of Award for Women Empowerment Activism in 2019. As she begins her five-year single term as UNIJOS’s first female substantive Vice-Chancellor after 55 years, she brings nearly four decades of institutional experience to the university’s top seat. entertainment.description: Nigerian sprint champions Praise Tejiri Ugoh, Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo, and Gift Bright celebrate their historic gold medal victories at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Photo Credit: MakingOfChamps Team Nigeria delivered an unforgettable chapter at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, wrapping up a historic multi-sport gathering that marked the first time an Olympic-branded event was ever hosted on African soil. Spanning across vibrant venues in Dakar, Diamniadio, and Saly, the Games brought together thousands of young athletes across 25 sports in a true celebration of youth culture, elite competition and unity. The grandeur of the international sporting festival kicked off with a breathtaking opening ceremony at the packed Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio. The night dazzled spectators with rich West African cultural displays, vibrant musical showcases, and a live performance by Nigerian music artist Ibquake , who brought incredible flair to the historic arena alongside global digital stars like Khaby Lame . Amidst the festive atmosphere, the Nigerian delegation walked with immense pride, led by sprint prodigy Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo carrying the national flag. Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo rejoices on the track wrapped in the green and white national flag after securing the women’s 100m gold. Photo Credit: MakingOfChamps/Instagram When the action shifted to the tracks at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop, Team Nigeria turned the athletics arena into a showcase of pure speed, finishing their campaign with a total of three medals—all of them gold. Fifteen-year-old Gift Bright set the blazing pace by conquering the men’s 100m final in a personal-best and Games-record time of 10.28 seconds, earning the distinction of becoming the first Nigerian men’s 100m champion at the Youth Olympics. Gift Bright powers down the track en route to winning the men’s 100m gold in a personal-best 10.28 seconds. The golden sweep was officially sealed by sixteen-year-old Praise Tejiri Ugoh , who stormed through the women’s 400m final in a personal-best time of 52.76 seconds to claim gold and become the first Nigerian to conquer the 400m distance at the Games. Praise Tejiri Ugoh claims gold for Nigeria on the podium following the women’s 400m final at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. sports.title: 'We did likewise': Mohit Ulva reveals why India celebrated aggressively after beating Pakistan
sports.description: India U-19 batter Mohit Ulva has explained the emotions behind the team's animated celebrations following their dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final, insisting that the players were simply celebrating their triumph and had no intention of provoking their opponents. Mohit, who played a decisive role in India's remarkable chase with an unbeaten 49 off just 26 balls, said the celebrations were a natural reaction to the occasion, given the intensity of an India-Pakistan contest and the fact that it was a final. The celebrations that followed, however, became a talking point, with several Indian players facing criticism on social media for their aggressive gestures towards the Pakistani players. Mohit revealed that the celebrations were a spontaneous expression of the emotions surrounding an India-Pakistan final. He also recalled how the Indian youngsters had not taken Pakistan's celebrations during the league-stage encounter personally. "It is natural. It was an India vs Pakistan match, and additionally, a final. The way they celebrated after beating us in the league stage. Actually, we were not even taking their celebration personally. We were thinking that they were celebrating their own victory. It doesn't matter what they do. "We did likewise. We were celebrating our own victory. It had emotions, aggression, and everything. We weren't doing it to show them anything. We were celebrating among ourselves, and everything was natural," Mohit told Star Sports. 'I couldn't believe I had finished it' India were staring at defeat after slipping to 252/8 in the 42nd over of the chase. However, Mohit and Manal Chauhan refused to give up, putting together a crucial 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket to keep India's hopes alive. Manal scored 47 off 32 balls before departing, leaving India needing 36 more runs with just one wicket remaining. Mohit then received support from No. 11 C Venkata, who remained unbeaten on 11 off eight deliveries. The equation eventually came down to three runs off the final ball, with Mohit finding the boundary to seal the title. Recalling the extraordinary finish, the youngster admitted that he was initially unable to process what had happened. "Actually, I was completely zoned out after hitting three runs on one ball with a four. I didn't know that everyone was running to me; everything was happening. "It was done; I finished the game. Until it was over, I believed that I would finish it. But after I did it, I couldn't believe that I had finished it. So, I was a little zoned out. "After a while, I realised that it was actually over. Everyone was getting up, everyone was celebrating. So, I celebrated a little. I went to the supporters of India, who were sitting there the whole day. I went to them and celebrated with them. It's a very good feeling. Even now, it's a very good feeling for me. Because for my family, for my country, for India, it's a good feeling to win such a match," he added. '

sports.title: Ciryl Gane Needs A Homecoming Fight In France After UFC 334
sports.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Ciryl Gane walked out of Madison Square Garden with his UFC heavyweight title intact on Saturday night. He defeated Josh Hokit by unanimous decision, but the reception felt wrong for a fighter who just set a new record for strikes in a single heavyweight bout. Gane landed 298 total strikes and Hokit threw 243, for a combined 541 strikes, which ESPN reported as a division record. The Frenchman displayed skill, but fans in the arena treated him like a villain rather than a champion. UFC CEO Dana White admitted he once thought Hokit was a “bigmouthed goofball” before the fight took place. White changed his tune after seeing Hokit push the champion backward with relentless pressure throughout the five-round war. “I respect the s— out of that guy,” White said during the postfight news conference, adding that Hokit is the real deal. By enduring Gane’s volume and electrifying the crowd with a massive slam to close the first round, Hokit earned this respect. A Homecoming in France Gane has spent years playing the role of the bad guy, even after beating top contenders like Alex Pereira in June. He lost to Jon Jones in 2023 and faced controversy with Francis Ngannou in 2022, but his résumé proves he belongs at the top. The UFC should stop booking him in hostile markets and finally give him a fight in his home country of France. As one of the top pound-for-pound fighters globally, Gane has constructed an impressive record and merits a cheering crowd. The Tactical Mistake in the Co-Main While Gane won the main event, Amanda Nunes made a costly tactical error in the co-main event against Kayla Harrison. The former two-time champion returned from retirement but was outplayed by the reigning bantamweight champion, who imposed her own game. Despite possessing the striking ability and experience to win, Nunes could not dictate the pace or terms of the engagement. Hokit said in his postfight interview that he will “rejoice in my suffering.” He promised that even if people kick him when he is down, he will still break their leg one day. Gane credited Hokit’s approach after the bout, noting that the world took him lightly but not the champion himself. “This guy is a motherf—er,” Gane said about his challenger. Gane landed 237 significant strikes, shattering the UFC heavyweight record for a single fight.

sports.title: Tottenham Hotspur Urged To Move In For This Arsenal Forward: Should De Zerbi Go For Him?

Is he exceptionally good in the air, is he a bully-type striker like Delap or is a clever front player, more like Havertz?” Gyokeres’ Growing Struggles In North London Gyokeres has struggled to earn regular first-team starts for Arsenal in this campaign so far as he has fallen behind Kai Havertz in Mikel Arteta’s pecking order. The 28-year-old registered two goals and three assists in 14 appearances for the Gunners this season in all competitions. The Swedish talent is currently among the most talented forwards in the Premier League. Hence, Tottenham would do well to bring him on board next year. We can expect Gyokeres to add more quality and depth to Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi’s frontline. He is capable of challenging for a regular first-team spot at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. At 28, Gyokeres is about to enter his prime, which makes him a decent choice for Spurs to pursue in 2027. Hence, Tottenham would be wise to go for a striker with his skill set soon.

sports.title: LeBron James Returns For Sixers As Back-To-Back Looms
sports.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James is set to return to the Philadelphia 76ers lineup for Sunday’s home game against the Indiana Pacers. The 41-year-old star missed Thursday’s victory over the Toronto Raptors to manage low back and sciatica issues, marking his third absence in the team’s first 13 games. This is a massive boost for a team that has struggled to find consistency without its veteran leader. The Sixers have been careful with James’ workload all season. He has not played on consecutive days yet this year as the team manages his health. Nick Nurse now faces a tough choice on how much to play him before the team travels to Brooklyn for a road game on Monday. James struggled in his last outing against Boston, scoring only 11 points on 4-of-12 shooting in 29 minutes. In his first season with the Sixers, he maintains averages of 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 6.5 assists across 10 appearances. His passing ability remains a key asset even if his scoring has dipped. A Tough Road Ahead The Pacers enter Sunday’s game looking for their third straight win after beating the New York Knicks in NBA Cup play on Friday. While dealing with their own injury concerns, Indiana has relied heavily on Pascal Siakam. The Sixers have managed to keep winning despite the heavy load on James and Joel Embiid. Tyrese Maxey led the team with 27 points in the win over Toronto, while Anfernee Simons added 17 off the bench. Rookie VJ Edgecombe also contributed 15 points, eight rebounds and eight assists in that game. Philadelphia has a difficult path in the NBA Cup after a heavy 24-point loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov. 6. That loss hurt their point differential significantly and put them behind in the group race. The team now needs big wins against tough opponents like the Heat and Pacers to stay in the hunt. Sixers Wire reports that the Sixers, Cavaliers, Heat, Knicks, and Pacers are among the teams battling for a next-round spot. The math for Philadelphia is unforgiving, and every point matters. Back-to-Back Concerns According to The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Chris Hine, Thursday’s absence was James’ first that was not related to a back-to-back schedule. This makes his availability for Monday’s game against the Brooklyn Nets a major question mark. The team must decide if playing Sunday is worth the risk of burning him out for the road trip. James has four full days of rest before Sunday, which gave him extra recovery time. LeBron James has not been officially confirmed as a starter yet, though his absence from the injury report suggests he is expected to play.

sports.title: Blues Offense Stalls Again In Ugly Loss To Florida
sports.description: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images A 4-1 loss to the Florida Panthers on Saturday night meant the St. Louis Blues could not achieve three straight wins. This loss dropped the team to 9-9-2 on the season, a record that makes it hard to call them a true contender. Jacob Markstrom recorded 21 saves for Florida as Dylan Holloway netted the single goal for St. Louis. Joel Hofer stopped 24 shots, but it was not enough to keep the game close. A Special Night with Ugly Results Saturday was supposed to be about celebrating Keith Tkachuk. Supporters had a chance to celebrate a legend as the Blues recognized his Hockey Hall of Fame induction. His sons, Matthew and Brady, played for the Panthers that night, adding a personal touch to the ceremony. Robert Thomas even wore a Tkachuk jersey to the arena, a nod to the time he lived with the family. The ceremonial faceoff used sticks Keith actually used during his career. It was a great moment for the family and the fans, but the result on the ice was a disaster. The team could not translate that emotional energy into goals. Offense Just Does Not Exist The Blues struggled to generate anything offensively from the start, managing just two shots on goal in the first period. Florida had 10 shots, and they capitalized on a pair of penalties to take an early lead. Brady Tkachuk opened the scoring with a toe drag, beating Hofer glove-side. Dmitry Kulikov made it 2-0 after a deflection off Colton Parayko’s stick. The second period offered no help, as St. Louis failed to register a single shot on its power play. For the seventh time this season, the Blues managed to score one goal or fewer. According to The Hockey News , they have now been outscored 16-6 in the four games where they tried to win three straight. “It’s something we’re trying to work on, right,” Blues forward Jake Neighbours said. “I wish I had the answer for you,” Neighbours added after playing in his 300th NHL game. Defense Breaks Down Fast Defensive mistakes doomed the Blues before the offense could even try to fix them. The Panthers scored early and often, building a lead the Blues could not chip away at. Anton Lundell added a goal in the second period, and Sam Reinhart made it 4-1 in the third with a slick move past Parayko. With one game remaining before the quarter mark, the team currently trails the second wild card spot in the Western Conference by three points. “More intensity and driving the net harder and getting pucks there more often,” Blues coach Jim Montgomery said. The team has two days to regroup before their next game. The Blues will look to finish off this two-game homestand strong when they come back Tuesday against Anaheim.

sports.title: NASCAR Drivers Lose Power Over Crew Chief Changes
sports.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Two of the biggest names in NASCAR admitted they had no voice in recent crew chief changes. Alex Bowman and Shane van Gisbergen confirmed they were not consulted before their teams swapped leaders. The moves happened right after the 2026 season ended, leaving drivers to accept new bosses they did not choose. This shift shows a clear power gap between the people behind the wheel and the teams that hire their staff. Drivers Feel Shut Out Alex Bowman, who is wrapping up his final Cup season in 2027, lost Blake Harris as his crew chief. Harris is moving to Trackhouse Racing to lead Shane van Gisbergen’s team. Bowman told Autoweek he was not part of the decision-making process. When questioned regarding his participation in the crew chief situation, “I haven’t really been a part of that,” Bowman replied, according to Autoweek . He added that other people likely have a better view of the changes. The Arizona native noted that not every race team operates the same way, which makes finding the right fit harder for drivers. Van Gisbergen faces a similar reality with his own crew chief, Stephen Doran, returning to Spire Motorsports. He described the process as simply accepting who you get and making it work. “You kind of just get put with who you are and work it out from there,” Van Gisbergen said. He believes the final call rests entirely with the team owners and managers. Why Leadership Matters More Because of this, he needs a crew chief who can step up and make tough calls. “I’m not the most natural leader in the world,” Bowman said. He explained that having a strong leader in the booth is vital for his success. “I’m shy and awkward and kind of stick to myself. So having a good, strong leader as a crew chief is important.” The changes ripple through the organization. Spire offered a team-wide engineering role to Travis Peterson, who had been Michael McDowell’s crew chief. Meanwhile, Austin Dillon will also have a new crew chief in 2027. Richard Childress Racing now has Richard Boswell as vice president of competition; he served Dillon for the last two seasons. These shifts happen fast, and the drivers are left to adapt or accept the outcome. Van Gisbergen summed up the situation with a simple statement about where the power lies. “It’s up to the team, I guess,” Van Gisbergen said. The lack of driver input is now a settled fact for the 2027 season.

sports.title: Today in White Sox History: November 15
sports.description: On this day 26 years ago, Frank Thomas has his third MVP “stolen” from him. | (Photo by DAVID MAXWELL/AFP via Getty Images) 1945 Harry Grabiner , the longest-tenured executive in White Sox history and certainly one of the longest-running employees overall, resigned as GM of the club. While not really formally holding a GM title, Grabiner had run the White Sox in tandem with three generations of Comiskey ownership, dating back to 1915. He first caught on with the team in 1905, selling scorecards; the 15-year-old got the job after noticing owner Charles Comiskey working the Comiskey Park infield after a rainstorm and asking if he could help out. By 1916, Grabiner was the team secretary (the de facto GM), at just 26. In 1939 upon the death of Comiskey’s son, Louis , the will stipulated that Grabiner was guaranteed another 10 years of employment in running the White Sox. However, Grabiner’s health was in decline, forcing his leave six years later. Grabiner would soon return to baseball, as part of Bill Veeck ’s ownership group in Cleveland. Meanwhile in Chicago, sabermetrics pioneer Les O’Connor took over the club for the next three seasons. Also on this day came some administrative news of a different sort. With Hall of Fame voting at this time occurring just once every three years, just one player and two people overall had been elected to the Hall of Fame over the previous five years. With a massive pileup of worthy players were clogging the ballot, Cooperstown decided to hold a runoff election in order to get more players into the Hall — but the move was ineffective, as no one reached the necessary 75% for election. That included legendary White Sox hurler Ed Walsh , who received just 137 of 247 (55.5%) of votes, finishing third overall on the ballot. 1948 After six years with the White Sox (interrupted right in the middle by three seasons lost to military service in World War II), Taffy Wright was sold to Philadelphia. Wright logged 12.5 in his White Sox career, was an average or better player in four of six seasons, and earned MVP votes in three. By 1948, with the right fielder’s WAR winnowed down to 0.5 over a full season of play, Chicago cut ties. He would play one subpar season for the Athletics and would not see the majors again, although Wright would stay active in the minors until 1956, at age 44. 1951 In an outrageous turn, White Sox outfielder Minnie Miñoso lost the American League Rookie of the Year award to Gil McDougald of the New York Yankees , 13 votes to 11. The polarizing heavyweight contender failed in his first attempt to become champion at UFC 334. Inside Madison Square Garden, Hokit was defeated by Ciryl Gane in the Frenchman’s first defence of the undisputed title. Many were rooting against the American owing to his controversial gimmick. But while the UFC president isn’t a fan of it, he was only focused on Hokit’s toughness after seeing his first five-rounder. Dana White has ‘nothing but respect’ for Josh Hokit after his UFC 334 battle with Ciryl Gane White was among those criticising Hokit when he made distasteful remarks about former First Lady Michelle Obama following his win on the White House lawn this past June. More recently, the UFC boss claimed to have matched Hokit with tough opponents because of his dislike for him. Those issues seem to be in the rear-view mirror now for White, who had strong praise for how Hokit performed at Madison Square Garden on November 14. “Listen, I’ve had my issues with Hokit, right?” White said at his post-event press conference in New York City. “Every fight, I was like, ‘This is the guy that’s (gonna beat him).’ “But think about this tonight too: Hokit’s first five-round main event, and he went five hard, crazy rounds. “The guy’s got an unbelievable chin, unstoppable cardio, and I give him nothing but respect for the fight that he fought tonight. It was incredible,” he added. Whether or not that means White will entertain Hokit’s request for a rematch with Gane remains to be seen. During the same press conference, the UFC president pointed to a grudge match against Alex Pereira as a “fun” next fight for him. First things first, ‘Poatan’ has a showdown with heavyweight knockout artist Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335 in December. sports.title: ‘You don’t even realise’: Bam Adebayo says one Miami Heat player is so good he can’t even ‘put it into words’
sports.description: Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images Giannis Antetokounmpo is usually the subject of all the praise when we’re talking about the Miami Heat, but there are other excellent players too. Bam Adebayo is definitely one of them, and after a difficult start, he has shown his class in the Heat’s last two games against the Pistons and the Cavaliers. Another player who has really shone this season is Klay Thompson, and Adebayo has heaped praise on him now. Bam Adebayo hails Miami Heat teammate Klay Thompson Thompson has quietly been magnificent for the Miami Heat this season. The 36-year-old has always been a good player, but he seems to have taken his game to a whole new level in recent games. Thompson has scored over 20 points in four different games this season, the latest of which came against the Pistons, where he scored 26 in just 20 minutes. That has earned him a lot of praise, and Adebayo has now joined the queue. He told 104.3 WQAM : “You can see what me and big fella (Giannis) are capable of, but Klay, man, he just adds a whole other dynamic to our team. “I don’t even know how to put it into words. Like sometimes, you don’t even realise he got 26 until you look up, and I’m like: ‘D***, when did he get 26?’ “You just start to be aware of the heater going on.” Thompson really has been the surprise package for the Miami Heat this season, and his performances have been more than welcome. At their best, we all know what Adebayo and Antetokounmpo can do, but if Thompson can keep knocking down 20+ points a game, the Heat could achieve something really special. Up next for Miami is an interesting game against the Houston Rockets. Back in April 2024, when he was with the Golden State Warriors, Thompson scored 29 points and recorded three rebounds and four assists against them. Heat fans would love for him to do the same on Monday night. sports.title: Arsenal Can Win the Champions League, But Let’s Not Get Carried Away
sports.description: Arsenal Can Win the Champions League, But Let’s Not Get Carried Away There’s a lot of talk among Arsenal fans and in the media about us winning the Champions League this season. I think we can all agree that we’d love to see Mikel Arteta’s side go one better than last season, when we finished runners-up to French giants PSG. But honestly, how realistic is that? It’s not impossible, of course, and we’re admittedly one of the competition’s favourites. Getting our hands on the trophy is obviously the aim. But I can’t say I feel overconfident this season, and I don’t think we should get too carried away in any competition. Fleetwood Was a Warning for Arsenal Anything can happen in football, as we certainly know after bowing out of the League Cup on penalties to League Two Fleetwood Town. They hadn’t even practised penalties before the game , and it was one of our worst displays in our entire history. If we get carried away in the Champions League, as perhaps we did in the League Cup, we could slip up once we get past the league phase, which we’ve started well. I’m not saying we should go in feeling like underdogs. But if we came up against PSG in the final again, or even Bayern Munich, who we arguably struggled against already this season, we could find ourselves on the losing end again. We haven’t established ourselves as one of the outright giants of the Champions League. We haven’t won European silverware in over 30 years, which the likes of Bayern, PSG, Liverpool, Real Madrid and Chelsea can’t relate to. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) PSG Showed How Far Arsenal Still Have to Go That has to be kept in perspective, but it shouldn’t dampen all our hopes either. I do think we were lucky to draw Atlético Madrid in the semis last season, having already beaten them in the competition. It was a tighter contest that time, but I don’t think we’d have reached the final if we’d come up against PSG instead. I can see them making this season’s final for a third time in a row. We struggled against PSG in the 2025 semi-final, and although we looked stronger against them in last season’s final , they still had us chasing shadows at times. They could’ve thrashed us in extra time, but we held out. We peaked too early when Kai Havertz gave us the lead inside the opening ten minutes, and it was 1-1 after extra time before we lost on penalties. For me, we didn’t really look like European winners that night. Even this season, we only just beat Slavia Prague 2-1, a side we should’ve scored three or four against on paper, if not more. It would be great to win the Champions League and retain the Premier League title this season. But let’s not get carried away! COYG!! Liam Harding Gooners, did reaching last season’s final convince you Arsenal are ready to win the Champions League, or did the performance against PSG show there’s still a gap to close? sports.description: There’s a lot of old timey baseball things that don’t exist in the modern MLB. One notable one is ties. Now, it’s not that they didn’t play extra innings back in the early decades, they did. The issue was that for a long time stadiums did not have lights. Eventually, things got to a point where you literally could not play anymore. Leagues like NPB in Japan still have ties, but MLB has specifically created rules (the extra innings automatic runner) to ensure that games don’t go too long and end with a winner. However, that wasn’t always the case. Sometimes, that could lead to some funny box scores, like this one from 1919. Very early in the 1919 season, the Yankees were hosting the Washington Senators on May 11th . The game that day was a makeup one after a scheduled meeting two days prior was postponed due to “wet grounds.” There’s another old timey baseball thing that you don’t really see today. The Yankees faced a difficult task that day as starting on the mound for Washington was future Hall of Famer Walter Johnson. However, Yankees starter Jack Quinn was up to the challenge himself, although it would be a difficult journey. In the second inning, the Senators put their first two runners on base thanks to a single and an error, but Quinn managed to work around that by getting two big strikeouts for the first two outs. That would become a pretty common occurrence for the Yankees on the day. In the third, Quinn allowed a single to Johnson himself, before getting out of the inning with a double play. science.title: 30 years ago, 'Space Jam' proposed the best way to resolve interplanetary disputes
science.description: null You just ordered a Pizza Hut and a two-liter bottle of Mountain Dew. You put on "Space Jam" to watch the greatest of all time team up with the Looney Tunes. It's a perfect evening… in 1996 or 2026. The entire concept of "Space Jam" is so '90s that you swear you can hear Los Del Rio in the background mouthing, "Dale a tu cuerpo alegría, Macarena." As ridiculous as an intergalactic basketball match may sound, it's a perfect example of how even the strangest idea can work if you commit to it fully. In case you thought you hallucinated the whole thing, no, you didn't, as the Looney Tunes find themselves in quite the predicament in this live-action-animation hybrid. A bunch of aliens known as the Nerdlucks arrive on Earth to abduct the Tunes and take them back as attractions to the outer-space amusement park known as Moron Mountain (shockingly nobody has claimed that subreddit, so do your thing, Internet!). Being a wheeling-and-dealing wabbit, though, Bugs Bunny proposes a winner-takes-all basketball game between the Tunes and the tiny Nerdlucks. Unfortunately, the crafty aliens use their tech to steal the talent from ballers like Charles Barkley and Muggsy Bogues and turn themselves into the scary and skilled Monstars. So, Bugs and friends reach out to Michael Jordan, who recently switched from basketball to baseball, to help the Tune Squad win this intergalactic b-ball matchup and their freedom, because if anybody can do it, Air Jordan (Hare Jordan?) can. Oh, Bill Murray also shows up here a few times. Why? Because he can! (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) "Space Jam" is a spin on the classic sci-fi trope of resolving high-stakes conflicts through sports. In 1975, "Death Race 2000" introduced a world where people drive like hooligans and bash into each other to get ahead and win races (ironically, this is the regular experience on any public road now). Meanwhile, in the same year, "Rollerball" demonstrated how to use extreme sports as a plot device whereby brutality trumped any kind of skill in the arena. Yet "Space Jam" took this concept, cartoonified it for a family-friendly audience, and challenged the conflict resolution approaches of other alien invasion movies from 1996. While " Independence Day " saw the heroes trying to destroy the mothership and "Mars Attacks" featured humans running away from "Ack! Ack"-ing extraterrestrials with ray guns, this film used the court to settle the score. It's an innovative way to deal with interplanetary matters, that's for sure. (Image credit: Warner Bros Pictures) Here's the thing: a basketball game is incredibly fair and puts everybody on equal footing. It isn't about who has the biggest guns or most high-tech spacecraft; it's about who can best work as a team to get a result. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
science.description: null On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) Why it mattered When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later. "In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus." The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO. The Green Bank Telescope collapse left a mass of twisted debris behind. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions. "One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
science.description: null For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to 1,000 times its usual brightness before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle. Why is it so challenging to predict T. CrB's nova flare? "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued. Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached Earth in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth. An animation of T. CrB brightening. (Image credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center Conceptual Image Lab) "The exact date of the upcoming T CrB eruption depends primarily on how fast the gas coming from its companion star is accumulating on the surface of the white dwarf," explained Schaefer. "When some specific trigger mass has accumulated, then T CrB will erupt. For the last 80 years, we have been watching the gas pile up on the white dwarf surface, and we know that it must be near the trigger threshold." Astronomers have tried to predict T CrB's brightening by comparing a recent fluctuation in the light of the distant star system to a similar event that occurred in the runup to the 1946 event. "There have already been some dimming and brightening episodes that caused excitement but did not yet turn into the main event," Elizabeth Hays, lab chief at NASA's Astroparticle Physics Laboratory at the Goddard Spaceflight Center , told Space.com in an email. "It is likely that the nova will happen in the next few years but we still don't know exactly when. I can't give you a guaranteed prediction, but I will be a little surprised if it gets to 2030, or 84 years past the last eruption." science.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
science.description: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year. On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit) , 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life. On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event. By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August. Telling the tale of a dirty snowball Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space. Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten. "We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a statement . science.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
science.description: null Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved. Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." The F light 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX. And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average. Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites . And its planned Starmind AI data-center constellation will be 10 times bigger than that, featuring one million spacecraft , if all goes to plan. For perspective: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network in low Earth orbit (LEO), by far the largest constellation ever assembled, is about 11,000 strong at the moment.
